explanation: Major agricultural and physiological applications of auxin hormones.

mnemonic: Bakanae Foolish Seedling, Kurosawa, Gibberella fujikuroi
bullets: Disease: 'Bakanae' (foolish seedling) in rice seedlings
Pathogen: Fungus Gibberella fujikuroi
Scientist: E. Kurosawa (1926) discovered active substance causing uninhibited stem elongation
explanation: Fungal origin discovery of gibberellic acid (GA3 as most common).

mnemonic: Bolting, Sugarcane Length, Malting, Delay Senescence
bullets: Bolting: Internode elongation prior to flowering in rosette plants (Beet, Cabbage)
Sugarcane Yield: Increases stem length, boosting yield by up to 20 tonnes/acre
Malting: Hastens malting process in brewing industry
Fruit Extension: Elongates & improves shape of apples; extends market period
explanation: Commercial uses of GA in agriculture, horticulture, and brewing industry. Chapter 13: Plant Growth and Development (30 Mnemonics) 	Page 2

mnemonic: Skoog Miller Kinetin Herring Sperm DNA
bullets: Scientists: F. Skoog and co-workers; isolated active substance by Miller et al.
Substance: Kinetin (N6-furfurylamino purine) crystallized from autoclaved herring sperm DNA
Note: Kinetin does not occur naturally in plants
explanation: Discovery history of adenyl purine derivate cytokines that stimulate cell division.

bullets: Isolation: Zeatin was isolated naturally from Corn kernels (Zea mays) & Coconut milk
Natural Sites: Synthesized in root apices, developing shoot buds, and young fruits
explanation: Naturally occurring plant cytokinin regulating shoot and cell proliferation.

mnemonic: Overcomes Apical Dominance, Chloroplasts, Delay Senescence
bullets: Overcomes Apical Dominance: Promotes growth of lateral buds into branches
Richmond-Lang Effect: Delays leaf senescence by promoting nutrient mobilization
Organogenesis: Promotes shoot formation, adventitious shoots, and new chloroplasts in leaves
explanation: Physiological roles of cytokinins in cell division, morphogenesis, and anti-aging.

topic: Auxin to Cytokinin Ratio in Organogenesis
mnemonic: High Auxin = Roots, High Cytokinin = Shoots
bullets: High Auxin / Low Cytokinin: Promotes Root differentiation in tissue culture
High Cytokinin / Low Auxin: Promotes Shoot formation in callus culture
Balanced Ratio: Promotes unorganized cell mass (Callus proliferation)
explanation: Hormonal balance controlling root/shoot organogenesis in plant tissue culture.

bullets: Scientist: H.H. Cousins (1910)
Experiment: Showed volatile substance from ripened oranges accelerated ripening of stored unripe bananas
Identity: Later identified as the gaseous hydrocarbon hormone Ethylene (C2H4)
explanation: Historical identification of ethylene as a natural gaseous plant ripening factor.

bullets: Response 1: Horizontal growth of seedlings
Response 2: Swelling of the axis (radial expansion)
Response 3: Apical hook formation in dicot seedlings
explanation: Bioassay response of dicot seedlings to ethylene exposure during germination. Chapter 13: Plant Growth and Development (30 Mnemonics) 	Page 3

bullets: Respiratory Climacteric: Rapid rise in respiration rate during fruit ripening
Abscission & Senescence: Promotes leaf/flower drop and female flowering in Cucumbers
Ethephon: Most widely used commercial compound releasing ethylene in aqueous solution (speeds ripening in tomatoes/apples, thin cotton/walnut)
explanation: Agricultural applications of ethylene gas and aqueous ethephon formulations.

topic: Ethylene Special Effects on Aquatic Plants & Seeds
mnemonic: Deep Water Rice Elongation, Peanut Germination, Pineapple Flowering
bullets: Deep Water Rice: Promotes rapid internode/petiole elongation to keep upper leaves above water
Seed/Bud Germination: Breaks seed dormancy in Peanuts and sprouting of Potato tubers
Pineapple: Synchronizes fruit set and induces flowering
explanation: Ecological and commercial adaptive effects of ethylene on specific crops.

bullets: Independent Isolations: Inhibitor-B, Abscisin II, and Dormin purified by three independent groups
Chemical Identity: All three proved chemically identical and named Abscisic Acid (ABA)
explanation: Convergence of three independent research tracks into the single stress hormone ABA.

mnemonic: Stomata Closure, Seed Dormancy, Antagonist to GA
bullets: Stomatal Closure: Stimulates rapid closure of stomata under water stress
Seed Maturation & Dormancy: Promotes seed development and induces dormancy to withstand desiccation
Antagonist: Acts as general growth inhibitor and direct antagonist to Gibberellins (GAs)
explanation: Primary survival functions of ABA during environmental abiotic stress conditions.

mnemonic: ABA vs GA (Dormancy), Auxin vs Cytokinin (Apical Dominance)
bullets: ABA vs GA: ABA maintains seed dormancy; GA breaks dormancy and promotes germination
Auxin vs Cytokinin: Auxin promotes apical dominance; Cytokinin overrides it to sprout lateral buds
explanation: Classical antagonistic plant growth regulator pairs controlling key physiological switches.

mnemonic: LDP High Light, SDP Low Light, DNP Neutral
bullets: Long Day Plants (LDP): Flower when light exposure exceeds critical photoperiod (e.g., Wheat, Radish)
Short Day Plants (SDP): Flower when light exposure is less than critical photoperiod (e.g., Soyabean, Chrysanthemum)
Day Neutral Plants (DNP): Flowering uninfluenced by day length exposure (e.g., Tomato, Cucumber, Maize)
explanation: Classification of plants based on light duration requirement for floral induction. Chapter 13: Plant Growth and Development (30 Mnemonics) 	Page 4

topic: Site of Perception for Photoperiodism & Florigen
mnemonic: Leaves Perceive Light, Florigen Moves to Apex
bullets: Perception Site: Leaves perceive light/dark duration (NOT the shoot apex)
Florigen Hypothesis: Hormonal stimulus (Florigen) synthesizes in leaves and migrates to shoot apex to induce flowering
explanation: Perceptual organ vs target site mechanism governing photoperiodic floral transition.

bullets: Requirement: Quantitative or qualitative dependence on exposure to low temperature (1°C – 7°C)
Function: Prevents precocious reproductive development late in growing season
Perception Site: Shoot apical meristem / active dividing cells perceive cold stimulus
explanation: Cold-induced acceleration of reproductive capacity in winter plant varieties.

mnemonic: Winter Wheat Barley Rye & Biennial Sugarbeet Cabbage Carrot
bullets: Winter Varieties: Wheat, Barley, Rye (planted in autumn, harvested summer)
Biennial Plants: Sugarbeet, Cabbage, Carrot (monocarpic plants flowering in second season after winter cold)
explanation: Crop examples exhibiting vernalization requirements for successful grain/seed yield.

mnemonic: Cold Forms Vernalin, High Heat Devernalizes
bullets: Vernalin: Hypothetical floral stimulus generated by cold treatment in apical meristem
Devernalization: Reversal of cold-induced vernalization state by immediate exposure to high temperatures
explanation: Hormonal hypothesis and temperature reversal phenomena of cold stratification.

mnemonic: Hard Coat, Chemical Inhibitors, Immature Embryo
bullets: Impermeable Seed Coat: Hard seed coats preventing water/O2 entry
Chemical Inhibitors: Presence of Abscisic acid (ABA), Phenolic acids, Para-ascorbic acid
Embryonic Immaturity: Undeveloped/dormant embryo requiring maturation period
explanation: Endogenous and exogenous factors preventing seed germination despite favorable environments.

bullets: Scarification: Mechanical rupture (sandpaper, knives) or chemical rupture (concentrated acid) of hard seed coat
Stratification: Subjecting seeds to chilling conditions or light exposure
Chemical Treatment: Application of Gibberellic Acid (GA3) or Nitrates to neutralize ABA
explanation: Artificial and natural techniques used to break seed dormancy in agricultural practices. Chapter 13: Plant Growth and Development (30 Mnemonics) 	Page 5

mnemonic: Simple-Body Surface, Earth-Cuticle, Insect-Trachea, Aquatic-Gills, Terrestrial-Lungs
bullets: Body Surface: Sponges, Coelenterates, Flatworms (simple diffusion)
Moist Cuticle / Skin: Earthworms and Amphibians (Cutaneous respiration)
Tracheal Tubes: Insects and Cockroaches
Branchial (Gills): Aquatic Arthropods, Molluscs, and Fishes
Pulmonic (Lungs): Reptiles, Birds, Mammals, and Adult Amphibians
explanation: Evolutionary progression of specialized respiratory structures across animal groups.

bullets: External Nostrils → Nasal Chamber → Nasopharynx
Larynx (Sound box / Cartilaginous box) → Trachea (Windpipe)
Primary/Secondary/Tertiary Bronchi → Terminal Bronchioles → Respiratory Alveoli
explanation: Sequential anatomical path taken by atmospheric air from external environment to exchange site.

mnemonic: T5 Divides Trachea, Incomplete C-shaped Rings
bullets: T5 Level: Trachea divides at the level of the 5th thoracic vertebra into right and left primary bronchi
Cartilaginous Rings: Incomplete hyaline C-shaped rings support trachea and primary/secondary/tertiary bronchi up to initial bronchioles
explanation: Anatomical position of tracheal bifurcation and non-collapsible structural support.

bullets: Conducting Part: Nostrils up to terminal bronchioles (transports air, humifies, warms, and filters dust)
Exchange Part: Alveoli and their ducts (site of actual diffusion of O2 and CO2 between blood and air)
explanation: Functional segregation of the human respiratory system into transport vs diffusion zones.

mnemonic: Outer Parietal Thorax, Inner Visceral Lung
bullets: Parietal Pleura: Outer membrane in contact with thoracic lining
Visceral Pleura: Inner membrane in contact with lung surface
Pleural Fluid: Reduces friction on the lung surface during breathing
explanation: Double-layered serous membrane structure enclosing and protecting human lungs.

mnemonic: Dorsal Vertebra, Ventral Sternum, Lateral Ribs, Lower Diaphragm
bullets: Dorsally: Vertebral column
Ventrally: Sternum (Breastbone)
Laterally: Ribs
Inferiorly: Dome-shaped Diaphragm
explanation: Anatomic boundaries forming the airtight thoracic enclosure essential for volume changes. Chapter 14: Breathing and Exchange of Gases (30 Mnemonics) 	Page 1

mnemonic: Active, Diaphragm Contracts Down, EICM Ribs Up, Volume Up, Pressure Down
bullets: Active Process: Requires ATP for muscle contraction
Diaphragm Contraction: Increases thoracic volume in antero-posterior axis
External Intercostal Muscles (EICM): Lifts ribs & sternum, increasing volume in dorso-ventral axis
Pressure Gradient: Intra-pulmonary pressure falls below atmospheric pressure (-1 mmHg)
explanation: Active mechanical changes generating negative pressure to draw air into lungs.

mnemonic: Passive, Relax Diaphragm & EICM, Volume Down, Pressure Up
bullets: Passive Process: Muscle relaxation without direct ATP expenditure during normal breathing
Diaphragm Relaxation: Returns to dome shape (antero-posterior volume decreases)
Intercostals Relax: Ribs and sternum return to original position (dorso-ventral volume decreases)
Pressure Gradient: Intra-pulmonary pressure exceeds atmospheric pressure, expelling air
explanation: Passive elastic recoil mechanism expelling air from the lungs.

bullets: Internal Intercostal Muscles (IICM): Pull ribs inward and downward
Abdominal Muscles: Contract to push diaphragm upward, further decreasing thoracic volume
explanation: Active muscle involvement during forceful, non-resting exhalation.

mnemonic: 12 to 16 Times per Minute, Measured by Spirometer
bullets: Normal Rate: Healthy adult breathes 12–16 times/minute
Spirometer: Diagnostic instrument used to measure lung volumes and assess pulmonary functions
explanation: Physiological breathing frequency baseline and primary clinical measurement tool.

mnemonic: TV 500 mL, Minute Rate 6000 to 8000 mL
bullets: Tidal Volume (TV): Volume inspired/expired during normal quiet breathing (~500 mL)
Minute Volume: 500 mL x (12–16 breaths) = 6000 to 8000 mL per minute
explanation: Base pulmonary volume per single resting breath and per minute calculation.

topic: Inspiratory Reserve Volume (IRV) & Expiratory Reserve Volume (ERV)
bullets: IRV: Additional volume of air a person can inspire by forcible inspiration (2500–3000 mL)
ERV: Additional volume of air a person can expire by forcible expiration (1000–1100 mL)
explanation: Quantification of extra lung reserves available above and below normal tidal volume. Chapter 14: Breathing and Exchange of Gases (30 Mnemonics) 	Page 2

mnemonic: RV 1100-1200 mL, Never Spirometer, Dead Space 150 mL
bullets: Residual Volume (RV): Volume remaining in lungs even after forcible expiration (1100–1200 mL)
Spirometer Limit: RV, FRC, and TLC CANNOT be measured directly by spirometry
Anatomical Dead Space: Air remaining in conducting ducts (~150 mL) unavailable for exchange
explanation: Irremovable baseline lung volume maintaining alveolar inflation and spirometric limitations.

bullets: Inspiratory Capacity (IC): TV + IRV (~3000–3500 mL)
Expiratory Capacity (EC): TV + ERV (~1500–1600 mL)
Functional Residual Capacity (FRC): ERV + RV (~2100–2300 mL)
Vital Capacity (VC): ERV + TV + IRV (~3500–4500 mL)
Total Lung Capacity (TLC): RV + ERV + TV + IRV = VC + RV (~5000–6000 mL)
explanation: Mathematical combinations of basic lung volumes defining functional pulmonary capacities.

topic: Factors Affecting Diffusion Rate across Membrane
mnemonic: Solubility, Partial Pressure, Surface Area, Thickness Inverse
bullets: Partial Pressure Gradient: Primary driving force for gas movement
Solubility of Gases: Higher solubility increases diffusion speed
Surface Area: Larger alveolar surface area increases rate
Membrane Thickness: Inversely proportional; thinner membrane increases diffusion rate
explanation: Physico-chemical parameters governing Fick's law of gas diffusion across respiratory membrane.

mnemonic: CO2 Twenty to Twenty-Five Times More Soluble Than O2
bullets: Ratio: CO2 solubility is 20–25 times higher than O2 solubility across diffusion membrane
Consequence: Amount of CO2 diffusing across membrane per unit difference in partial pressure is much higher than O2
explanation: Fundamental solubility disparity between respiratory gases across biological membranes.

bullets: Layer 1: Thin squamous epithelium of alveoli
Layer 2: Endothelium of alveolar capillaries
Layer 3: Basement substance separating them
Total Thickness: Much less than 1 mm (0.2 mm) for rapid diffusion
explanation: Microscopic three-layered blood-air barrier architecture.

topic: Partial Pressure Values (pO2 & pCO2 Key Sites)
mnemonic: pO2: Air 159, Alveoli 104, Deox 40, Ox 95, Tissues 40
bullets: Atmospheric Air: pO2 = 159, pCO2 = 0.3 mmHg
Alveoli: pO2 = 104, pCO2 = 40 mmHg
Deoxygenated Blood: pO2 = 40, pCO2 = 45 mmHg
Oxygenated Blood: pO2 = 95, pCO2 = 40 mmHg
Tissues: pO2 = 40, pCO2 = 45 mmHg
explanation: Exact partial pressure gradients driving oxygen entry and carbon dioxide removal. Chapter 14: Breathing and Exchange of Gases (30 Mnemonics) 	Page 3

mnemonic: 97 Percent RBC Hemoglobin, 3 Percent Plasma Dissolved
bullets: Bound State: 97% of O2 transported by Red Blood Cells as Oxyhemoglobin
Dissolved State: 3% of O2 transported in dissolved state through blood plasma
explanation: Proportional distribution of oxygen transport forms in human arterial blood.

topic: Oxygen Binding Capacity per Gram Hb & 100 mL Blood
mnemonic: 1.34 mL per Gram Hb, 5 mL O2 Delivered per 100 mL Blood
bullets: Per Gram Hb: 1 gram of hemoglobin binds ~1.34 mL O2
Per 100 mL Oxygenated Blood: Carries ~20 mL O2, delivers 5 mL O2 to tissues under normal physiological conditions
explanation: Quantitative oxygen-carrying and tissue delivery metrics of circulating hemoglobin.

bullets: Curve Shape: Sigmoid curve when % saturation of Hb is plotted against pO2
P50 Value: Partial pressure of O2 at which Hb is 50% saturated (~30 mmHg in humans)
Binding Limit: 1 Hb molecule reversibly binds up to 4 O2 molecules
explanation: S-shaped binding affinity curve reflecting cooperative oxygen binding to hemoglobin tetramer.

topic: Factors Shifting O2-Hb Curve to RIGHT (Bohr Effect)
mnemonic: CADET Face Right = CO2, Acid (H+), DPG, Exercise, Temp
bullets: C: High pCO2
A: Acidic / High H+ (Low pH)
D: High 2,3-DPG
E: Exercise
T: High Temperature & Low pO2
Tissue Effect: Unloads O2 readily to metabolizing tissues (Bohr Effect)
explanation: Physiological conditions lowering Hb affinity for O2 and favoring oxygen release at tissues.

topic: Factors Shifting O2-Hb Curve to LEFT (Alveolar Level)
mnemonic: High pO2, Low pCO2, Low Temp, Low H+ (High pH)
bullets: Conditions: High pO2, Low pCO2, Low H+ concentration (Higher pH), Lower temperature
Location: Exists at Alveolar surface
Result: Increases Hb affinity for O2, promoting Oxyhemoglobin formation
explanation: Alveolar environmental parameters maximizing oxygen loading onto hemoglobin.

bullets: Bicarbonate (HCO3-): 70% transported as bicarbonate ions in plasma
Carbamino-Hemoglobin: 20–25% bound directly to amine group of hemoglobin
Dissolved State: 7% dissolved directly in plasma liquid
explanation: Three distinct chemical mechanisms handling systemic CO2 removal. Chapter 14: Breathing and Exchange of Gases (30 Mnemonics) 	Page 4

mnemonic: Carbonic Anhydrase RBC Zn2+, Chloride In at Tissues
bullets: Carbonic Anhydrase: Fastest enzyme (contains Zn2+), present in high concentration in RBCs
Reaction: CO2 + H2O <=> H2CO3 <=> HCO3- + H+
Hamburger Shift: HCO3- diffuses out of RBC at tissue level; Cl- shifts IN to maintain electrical neutrality
Reverse Shift: Cl- shifts OUT of RBC at alveolar capillaries
explanation: Enzymatic mechanism and ionic equilibrium exchange sustaining 70% CO2 transport.

topic: CO2 Delivery Volume per 100 mL Blood
mnemonic: 4 mL CO2 Delivered to Alveoli per 100 mL Deoxygenated Blood
bullets: Volume: Every 100 mL of deoxygenated blood delivers approximately 4 mL of CO2 to the alveoli for exhalation
explanation: Quantitative measurement of carbon dioxide gas eliminated per unit volume of venous blood.

topic: Respiratory Rhythm Center vs Pneumotaxic Center
mnemonic: Medulla Sets Rhythm, Pons Pneumotaxic Switches Off
bullets: Medulla Oblongata: Contains Respiratory Rhythm Center (primary regulator)
Pons Varolii: Contains Pneumotaxic Center (can send signals to reduce duration of inspiration & alter rate)
explanation: Brainstem neural centers co-ordinating autonomic respiratory frequency and depth.

mnemonic: Sensitive to CO2 & H+, Oxygen Insignificant!
bullets: Central Chemosensitive Area: Adjacent to rhythm center; highly sensitive to CO2 and H+ ions
Peripheral Receptors: Aortic arch and Carotid artery receptors detect CO2 and H+ levels
Role of Oxygen: Role of oxygen in regulation of respiratory rhythm is INSIGNIFICANT
explanation: Chemical feedback loop driven primarily by carbon dioxide/pH changes rather than oxygen deprivation.

mnemonic: Asthma Wheezing Inflammation, Emphysema Cigarette Surface Loss
bullets: Asthma: Difficulty breathing causing wheezing due to inflammation of bronchi and bronchioles
Emphysema: Chronic disorder where alveolar walls are damaged, decreasing respiratory surface area; major cause is Cigarette Smoking
explanation: Pathophysiological differences between obstructive airway hypersensitivity and alveolar wall destruction.

bullets: Industries: Stone-breaking and stone-grinding industries with long exposure to dust
Pathology: Causes severe inflammation leading to Fibrosis (proliferation of fibrous tissues) and lung damage
Examples: Silicosis and Asbestosis; protective masks required
explanation: Inhalation diseases caused by long-term workplace dust exposure causing irreversible lung scarring. Chapter 14: Breathing and Exchange of Gases (30 Mnemonics) 	Page 5

topic: Components of Blood (Plasma vs Formed Elements)
bullets: Plasma (55%): Liquid matrix containing 90-92% water and 6-8% proteins
Formed Elements (45%): Erythrocytes (RBCs), Leucocytes (WBCs), and Platelets (Thrombocytes)
explanation: Proportional division of total blood volume into fluid matrix and cellular components.

mnemonic: Fibrinogen Clots, Globulin Defends, Albumin Osmotic Balance
bullets: Fibrinogen: Needed for blood clotting / coagulation
Globulins: Involved in defense mechanisms (immunoglobulins/antibodies)
Albumins: Maintains osmotic balance and colloid osmotic pressure
explanation: Primary functions of the three major plasma protein fractions.

topic: Relative Abundance of White Blood Cells (WBC Abundance)
bullets: N (Neutrophils): 60 – 65% (Most abundant)
L (Lymphocytes): 20 – 25%
M (Monocytes): 6 – 8%
E (Eosinophils): 2 – 3%
B (Basophils): 0.5 – 1% (Least abundant)
explanation: Decreasing order of concentration for leucocyte types in normal human blood.

mnemonic: Gran Grandpa BEN, Agran Lympho Mono
bullets: Granulocytes: Basophils, Eosinophils, Neutrophils (contain cytoplasmic granules)
Agranulocytes: Lymphocytes, Monocytes (lack cytoplasmic granules)
explanation: Histological division of white blood cells based on presence of cytoplasmic granules.

mnemonic: Neutro-Mono Phagocytes, Baso Inflame, Eosino Allergy, Lympho Immunity
bullets: Neutrophils & Monocytes: Phagocytic cells destroying foreign organisms
Basophils: Secrete Histamine, Serotonin, Heparin; involved in inflammatory reactions
Eosinophils: Resist infections and associated with allergic reactions
Lymphocytes: B and T cells responsible for immune responses
explanation: Key physiological roles of distinct white blood cell types in immune defense.

mnemonic: 5 to 5.5 Million, Spleen Graveyard, Biconcave No Nucleus
bullets: Count: 5.0 to 5.5 million/mm3 of blood
Features: Enucleate (lacks nucleus in mammals), biconcave shape, 120 days lifespan
Destruction Site: Spleen is known as the graveyard of RBCs
Hemoglobin: 12–16 g of Hb per 100 mL of healthy blood
explanation: Structural, quantitative, and lifecycle parameters of red blood cells. Chapter 15: Body Fluids and Circulation (30 Mnemonics) 	Page 1

bullets: Origin: Cell fragments produced from Megakaryocytes (special cells in bone marrow)
Normal Count: 1,50,000 to 3,50,000 platelets/mm3 of blood
Function: Release coagulation substances; reduction leads to clotting disorders and excess blood loss
explanation: Cellular origin, normal count range, and physiological significance of platelets.

mnemonic: Antigen on RBC, Antibody in Plasma
bullets: Group A: A antigen on RBC, anti-B antibody in plasma
Group B: B antigen on RBC, anti-A antibody in plasma
Group AB: Both A & B antigens, NO antibodies (Universal Recipient)
Group O: NO antigens, Both anti-A & anti-B antibodies (Universal Donor)
explanation: Distribution of surface glycoproteins and plasma immunoglobulins defining ABO compatibility.

mnemonic: O Negative Universal Donor, AB Positive Universal Recipient
bullets: Universal Donor: O negative (O-ve) because it lacks A, B, and Rh antigens
Universal Recipient: AB positive (AB+ve) because it lacks anti-A, anti-B, and anti-Rh antibodies
explanation: Precise Rh and ABO blood subtypes for emergency universal transfusions.

mnemonic: Rh Negative Mother, Rh Positive Foetus, Anti-Rh Antibodies Kill
bullets: Condition: Rh -ve mother carrying Rh +ve foetus
Sensitization: Blood mixing during 1st delivery causes mother to form anti-Rh antibodies
Subsequent Pregnancy: Anti-Rh antibodies cross placenta and destroy fetal RBCs causing severe anemia & jaundice
Prevention: Administer Anti-Rh antibodies (RhOGAM) to mother immediately after 1st delivery
explanation: Incompatibility condition leading to fetal hemolytic anemia and preventive immunotherapy.

mnemonic: Thrombokinase converts Prothrombin to Thrombin, Thrombin converts Fibrinogen to Fibrin
bullets: Step 1: Damaged tissues/platelets release Thromboplastin forming enzyme complex Thrombokinase
Step 2: Prothrombin --(Thrombokinase + Ca2+)--> Thrombin
Step 3: Fibrinogen --(Thrombin)--> Fibrin threads (mesh capturing dead elements)
explanation: Sequential enzymatic cascade converting soluble plasma proteins into an insoluble fibrin clot.

topic: Key Ion Required for Blood Clotting
mnemonic: Calcium Ion (Ca2+) is Crucial for Clotting
bullets: Role: Calcium ions (Ca2+) play an essential role in multiple steps of the coagulation cascade
Clinical: Anticoagulants like EDTA or Sodium Citrate bind Ca2+ to prevent clotting in stored blood
explanation: Essential cofactor role of divalent calcium ions in hemostasis. Chapter 15: Body Fluids and Circulation (30 Mnemonics) 	Page 2

mnemonic: Colorless, Fewer Proteins, High Lymphocytes, Fats in Lacteals
bullets: Nature: Colorless interstitial fluid containing specialized lymphocytes
Composition: Similar to plasma but with lower protein concentration
Fat Transport: Digested fats are absorbed into lymph in lacteals present in intestinal villi
explanation: Features and transport roles of lymphatic fluid linking tissue space to circulation.

bullets: 2-Chambered (1 Atrium + 1 Ventricle): Fishes (Single circulation)
3-Chambered (2 Atria + 1 Ventricle): Amphibians and Reptiles (Incomplete double circulation)
4-Chambered (2 Atria + 2 Ventricles): Birds, Mammals, and Crocodiles (Complete double circulation)
explanation: Comparative evolution of cardiac chambers across vertebrate classes.

bullets: Origin: Mesodermally derived organ
Location: Thoracic cavity, in mediastinum between two lungs, tilted slightly to the left
Protection: Enclosed by double-walled membrane bag called Pericardium filled with pericardial fluid
explanation: Embryonic origin, anatomical position, and protective membrane of human heart.

mnemonic: Tricuspid Right, Bicuspid (Mitral) Left, Semilunar Outlets
bullets: Tricuspid Valve: Between Right Atrium and Right Ventricle
Bicuspid / Mitral Valve: Between Left Atrium and Left Ventricle
Semilunar Valves: At openings of Right Ventricle into Pulmonary Artery and Left Ventricle into Aorta
explanation: Anatomical locations of heart valves enforcing unidirectional blood flow.

mnemonic: SAN -> AVN -> AV Bundle (Bundle of His) -> Purkinje Fibres
bullets: SAN (Sino-atrial Node): Right upper corner of right atrium; Pacemaker (70–75 beats/min)
AVN (Atrio-ventricular Node): Lower left corner of right atrium near AV septum
AV Bundle & Purkinje Fibres: Transmit action potential rapidly through ventricular musculature
explanation: Sequential pathway of specialized auto-excitable cardiac tissue generating heart rate.

mnemonic: Atrial Systole 0.1s, Ventricular Systole 0.3s, Joint Diastole 0.4s (Total 0.8s)
bullets: Total Cycle Duration: 0.8 seconds (at standard 75 beats per minute)
Atrial Systole: 0.1 sec (increases blood flow to ventricles by ~30%)
Ventricular Systole: 0.3 sec (pumps blood into pulmonary artery and aorta)
Joint Diastole: 0.4 sec (all 4 chambers in relaxed state filling with blood)
explanation: Time distribution of atrial and ventricular mechanical events during one cardiac cycle. Chapter 15: Body Fluids and Circulation (30 Mnemonics) 	Page 3

mnemonic: Stroke Volume 70 mL, Cardiac Output = SV x HR = 5 Litres
bullets: Stroke Volume (SV): Volume of blood pumped by each ventricle per beat (~70 mL)
Cardiac Output (CO): SV x Heart Rate (70 mL x 72 beats/min = ~5000 mL or 5 Litres/min)
Variation: Athletes have significantly higher stroke volume and cardiac output
explanation: Mathematical relationship between stroke volume, heart rate, and total minute output.

mnemonic: LUB = AV Valves Close, DUB = Semilunar Valves Close
bullets: 1st Sound (LUB): Caused by closure of Tricuspid and Bicuspid valves at onset of Ventricular Systole
2nd Sound (DUB): Caused by closure of Semilunar valves at onset of Ventricular Diastole
explanation: Acoustic origins of normal cardiac stethoscope sounds.

mnemonic: P = Atrial Depolarisation, QRS = Ventricular Depolarisation, T = Ventricular Repolarisation
bullets: P-wave: Depolarisation (excitation) of atria leading to atrial contraction
QRS Complex: Depolarisation of ventricles initiating ventricular contraction
T-wave: Repolarisation of ventricles (return from excited to normal state)
Pulse Counting: Counting QRS complexes in a given time period gives heart rate
explanation: Standard electrocardiographic wave deflections mapped to cardiac electrical cycles.

mnemonic: Three Leads = Both Wrists + Left Ankle
bullets: Standard Lead Setup: Patient connected to 3 electrical leads
Attachments: One to each wrist (left and right) and one to the left ankle for continuous monitoring
explanation: Clinical positioning of standard three-lead monitoring electrodes.

mnemonic: Digestive Tract -> Hepatic Portal Vein -> Liver -> Vena Cava
bullets: Definition: Unique vascular connection between digestive tract and liver
Hepatic Portal Vein: Carries blood from intestine directly to liver before reaching systemic circulation
explanation: Specialized venous portal network routing nutrient-rich intestinal blood through liver first.

bullets: Function: Dedicated system of blood vessels (Coronary Arteries & Veins) exclusively supplying circulation to the heart muscle (Myocardium)
explanation: Specialized vascular network providing oxygen and nutrients to cardiac tissue itself. Chapter 15: Body Fluids and Circulation (30 Mnemonics) 	Page 4

bullets: Sympathetic Nerves: Release Noradrenaline; increases HR, strength of ventricular contraction, and cardiac output
Parasympathetic Nerves (Vagus): Release Acetylcholine; decreases HR, speed of conduction, and cardiac output
Neural Center: Located in Medulla Oblongata
explanation: Dual autonomic neural modulation balancing cardiac rate and force of contraction.

mnemonic: Adrenal Medulla Hormones Increase Cardiac Output
bullets: Hormones: Adrenaline (Epinephrine) and Noradrenaline from Adrenal Medulla
Effect: Increases heart rate, stroke volume, and overall cardiac output during emergency/fight-or-flight states
explanation: Endocrine control mechanism elevating cardiovascular parameters during stress.

bullets: Normal BP: 120 mmHg (Systolic) / 80 mmHg (Diastolic)
Hypertension: Repeated readings of 140/90 mmHg or higher
Consequences: Leads to heart diseases and affects vital organs like brain and kidney
explanation: Clinical diagnostic thresholds and target organ complications of high blood pressure.

mnemonic: Atherosclerosis = Calcium, Fat, Cholesterol Narrowing Lumen
bullets: Cause: Deposits of Calcium, Fat, Cholesterol, and fibrous tissues in coronary arteries
Pathology: Narrows the lumen of arteries supplying blood to heart muscle
explanation: Pathological narrowing of coronary arteries obstructing myocardial perfusion.

mnemonic: Acute Chest Pain, Lack of Oxygen to Heart Muscle
bullets: Symptom: Acute chest pain appearing when not enough oxygen reaches heart muscle
Demographics: Can occur in men and women of any age but more common in middle-aged and elderly
explanation: Ischemic symptom presenting as severe retrosternal chest pain during exertion/stress.

topic: Heart Failure vs Cardiac Arrest vs Heart Attack
mnemonic: Failure = Ineffective Pump, Arrest = Heart Stops Beating, Attack = Muscle Damaged
bullets: Heart Failure: Heart doesn't pump blood effectively enough to meet body needs (often called congestive heart failure due to lung congestion)
Cardiac Arrest: Heart completely stops beating due to electrical failure
Heart Attack (Myocardial Infarction): Heart muscle is suddenly damaged by an inadequate blood supply
explanation: Clinical differentiation between cardiac pump dysfunction, electrical cessation, and acute ischemia. Chapter 15: Body Fluids and Circulation (30 Mnemonics) 	Page 5

topic: Modes of Excretion (Toxicity & Water Loss Order)
mnemonic: Ammonia High Toxicity Water, Uric Acid Least Toxicity Paste
bullets: Ammonotelism: Ammonia is most toxic, requires maximum water for excretion
Ureotelism: Urea is moderately toxic, requires moderate water
Uricotelism: Uric acid is least toxic, excreted as pellet/paste with minimum water loss
explanation: Comparative toxicity ranking and water requirement order of the three major nitrogenous wastes.

mnemonic: Bony Fishes, Aquatic Amphibians, Aquatic Insects
bullets: Bony Fishes (Teleosts)
Aquatic Amphibians (e.g., Tadpole of Frog)
Aquatic Insects
Diffusion: Ammonia diffuses across body surface or gill surfaces as ammonium ions (NH4+)
explanation: Organisms living in abundant water environments that excrete highly soluble ammonia directly.

mnemonic: Mammals, Terrestrial Amphibians, Marine Fishes - Urea Made in Liver
bullets: Organisms: Mammals, terrestrial amphibians (adult frog), and marine fishes (cartilaginous)
Site: Ammonia converted into Urea in the LIVER (via Ornithine Cycle) and released into blood
explanation: Taxa that convert ammonia to less toxic urea in hepatic tissue to conserve water.

bullets: R: Reptiles
B: Birds (Aves)
L: Land Snails (Gastropods)
I: Insects (e.g., Cockroach)
explanation: Terrestrial organisms excreting nitrogenous waste as insoluble uric acid pellets to minimize water loss.

mnemonic: Flame Platy, Nephridia Annelida, Malpighian Arthro, Antennal Crustacean
bullets: Flame cells (Protonephridia): Platyhelminthes (Flatworms), Rotifers, Cephalochordate (Amphioxus)
Nephridia: Earthworms and other Annelids
Malpighian Tubules: Insects (Cockroach)
Antennal / Green Glands: Crustaceans (Prawns)
explanation: Invertebrate evolutionary specialization of excretory organs mapped to respective phyla.

mnemonic: T12 to L3, 10-12 cm Long, 120-170 g Weight
bullets: Vertebral Level: Between 12th thoracic (T12) and 3rd lumbar (L3) vertebrae
Length: 10 – 12 cm | Width: 5 – 7 cm | Thickness: 2 – 3 cm
Average Weight: 120 – 170 grams
explanation: Anatomical position on posterior abdominal wall and physical dimensions of human kidney. Chapter 16: Excretory Products and Their Elimination (30 Mnemonics) 	Page 1

topic: Internal Structure of Kidney (Cortex vs Medulla)
mnemonic: Outer Cortex, Inner Medullary Pyramids, Columns of Bertini
bullets: Cortex: Outer zone extending between medullary pyramids as Columns of Bertini
Medulla: Inner zone divided into a few conical medullary pyramids projecting into calyces
Renal Pelvis: Funnel-shaped space inner to hilum with extensions called calyces
explanation: Zonal anatomy of kidney parenchyma and urine collection pathways into pelvis.

mnemonic: Bowman -> PCT -> Henle (Desc/Asc) -> DCT -> Collecting Duct
bullets: Malpighian Body: Glomerulus (tuft of capillaries) + Bowman's capsule
Renal Tubule Pathway: Bowman's capsule → PCT → Loop of Henle → DCT → Collecting Duct
explanation: Sequential functional units comprising a single mammalian nephron.

mnemonic: Cortical Short Henle 85%, Juxtamedullary Long Henle Vasa Recta 15%
bullets: Cortical Nephrons (85%): Short loop of Henle extending only slightly into medulla; Vasa recta reduced/absent
Juxtamedullary Nephrons (15%): Long loop of Henle running deep into medulla; well-developed Vasa recta
explanation: Structural and numerical comparison between the two nephron populations.

topic: Blood Supply to Nephron (Afferent vs Efferent Arteriole & Vasa Recta)
mnemonic: Afferent Enters Wide, Efferent Exits Narrow, Peritubular Vasa Recta
bullets: Afferent Arteriole: Fine branch of renal artery entering Bowman's capsule (wider lumen)
Efferent Arteriole: Emerges from glomerulus (narrower lumen, creates glomerular hydrostatic pressure)
Peritubular Capillaries: Network around PCT/DCT giving off parallel U-shaped Vasa Recta loop
explanation: Vascular layout around nephron tubule generating pressure gradients and counter-current exchangers.

mnemonic: Glomerular Filtration, Tubular Reabsorption, Tubular Secretion
bullets: Step 1: Glomerular Filtration (Ultrafiltration)
Step 2: Reabsorption (Selective return of water and solutes to blood)
Step 3: Secretion (Active transport of H+, K+, NH3 into filtrate)
explanation: Three fundamental renal processes converting blood plasma into final excreted urine.

mnemonic: GFR 125 mL/min = 180 Litres/day, Urine 1.5 Litres/day (99% Reabsorbed)
bullets: GFR Value: 125 mL/minute = 180 Litres per day formed by both kidneys
Excreted Urine: ~1.5 Litres per day
Deduction: ~99% of filtrate is reabsorbed by renal tubules
explanation: Quantitative disparity between initial ultrafiltrate volume and final voided urine volume. Chapter 16: Excretory Products and Their Elimination (30 Mnemonics) 	Page 2

mnemonic: Glomerular Endothelium, Basement Membrane, Podocyte Epithelium
bullets: Layer 1: Endothelium of glomerular blood vessels
Layer 2: Basement membrane in between
Layer 3: Epithelium of Bowman's capsule (Podocytes with filtration slits/slit pores)
explanation: Triple-layered sieve responsible for ultrafiltration of blood plasma excluding proteins.

mnemonic: PCT = 70-80% Electrolytes & Water, 100% Glucose & Amino Acids, Brush Border
bullets: Surface: Simple cuboidal brush border epithelium increases surface area
Reabsorption: Nearly 100% of glucose & amino acids, and 70–80% of electrolytes and water
Secretion: Secretes H+, K+, and NH3 to maintain pH and ionic balance
explanation: Primary tubule segment responsible for bulk reabsorption of essential nutrients and electrolytes.

topic: Function of Loop of Henle (Descending vs Ascending Limbs)
mnemonic: Descending Permeable to Water, Ascending Permeable to Electrolytes
bullets: Descending Limb: Permeable to water, impermeable to electrolytes (filtrate becomes hypertonic)
Ascending Limb: Impermeable to water, active/passive transport of electrolytes (filtrate becomes hypotonic)
explanation: Differential permeability properties along Henle's loop producing medullary osmotic gradient.

topic: Reabsorption & Secretion in Distal Convoluted Tubule (DCT)
mnemonic: DCT = Conditional Na+ and Water Reabsorption, HCO3- Reabsorption
bullets: Conditional Reabsorption: Na+ and Water reabsorbed under hormonal influence (Aldosterone)
Acid-Base Balance: Reabsorbs HCO3- and selectively secretes H+, K+, and NH3
explanation: Fine-tuning segment regulated hormonally for homeostatic fluid balance and pH maintenance.

mnemonic: Large Water Reabsorption, Small Urea Pass to Medulla
bullets: Water Extraction: Reabsorbs large amounts of water to produce concentrated urine
Osmolality: Allows passage of small amounts of Urea into medullary interstitium to maintain gradient
explanation: Final tubular segment adjusting final urine concentration before emptying into calyces.

mnemonic: Opposite Flow in Henle & Vasa Recta Creates Medullary Gradient
bullets: Counter-Current Flow: Flow of filtrate in two limbs of Loop of Henle in opposite directions
Vasa Recta Flow: Flow of blood through two limbs of Vasa Recta also in opposite directions
Gradient: Increases osmolality from 300 mOsmol/L in cortex to 1200 mOsmol/L in inner medulla
explanation: Anatomical orientation enabling hyperosmolar medullary interstitial gradient maintenance. Chapter 16: Excretory Products and Their Elimination (30 Mnemonics) 	Page 3

bullets: NaCl Transport: Transported by ascending limb of Henle's loop and exchanged with descending limb of Vasa Recta
Urea Recycling: Enters thin ascending limb of Henle's loop and returned to interstitium by collecting duct
explanation: Two primary solutes recycled between tubules and vasa recta to preserve hypertonicity.

mnemonic: Human Kidneys Concentrate Urine 4 Times (1200 vs 300 mOsmol/L)
bullets: Initial Filtrate: 300 mOsmol/L (Isotonic to blood plasma)
Concentrated Urine: 1200 mOsmol/L (4x more concentrated than initial filtrate)
explanation: Maximum concentration factor achievable by human counter-current system for water conservation.

mnemonic: Osmoreceptors Hypothalamus -> Neurohypophysis ADH -> DCT Water Reabsorption
bullets: Trigger: Excessive fluid loss stimulates osmoreceptors in hypothalamus
Release: Neurohypophysis (posterior pituitary) releases ADH / Vasopressin
Action: Facilitates water reabsorption from DCT and Collecting duct, preventing diuresis
Feedback: Increase in body fluid volume switches off osmoreceptors
explanation: Endocrine reflex arc preventing dehydration via antidiuretic hormone secretion.

mnemonic: JGA = Cellular Modification at DCT Contact + Afferent Arteriole
bullets: Location: Sensitive region formed by cellular modifications at point of contact between DCT and Afferent arteriole
JG Cells: Release Renin enzyme in response to fall in glomerular blood flow / GFR
explanation: Anatomical auto-regulatory sensory complex monitoring renal blood flow and arterial pressure.

mnemonic: Renin -> Angiotensinogen to I -> Angiotensin II -> Vasoconstriction + Aldosterone
bullets: Low GFR: JG cells release Renin
Renin: Converts Angiotensinogen in blood to Angiotensin I and then Angiotensin II
Angiotensin II: Powerful vasoconstrictor (increases glomerular BP) + stimulates Adrenal Cortex to release Aldosterone
Aldosterone: Causes Na+ and water reabsorption in DCT, restoring GFR
explanation: Multihormonal feedback pathway restoring depressed blood pressure and glomerular filtration.

mnemonic: High BP -> Heart Atria Release ANF -> Vasodilation -> Lowers BP
bullets: Stimulus: Increase in blood flow to atria of heart
Action: ANF causes vasodilation (dilation of blood vessels) and inhibits Renin release
Result: Decreases blood pressure; acts as a check on RAAS mechanism
explanation: Cardiac hormone acting as a safety brake to prevent excessive hypertension caused by RAAS. Chapter 16: Excretory Products and Their Elimination (30 Mnemonics) 	Page 4

mnemonic: Stretch Receptors -> CNS -> Motor Signal -> Detrusor Contracts + Sphincter Relaxes
bullets: Stimulus: Urine fills bladder, stretching bladder wall
CNS Signal: Stretch receptors send signals to CNS
Motor Reflex: CNS signals contraction of smooth muscles of bladder and simultaneous relaxation of urethral sphincter
explanation: Neural reflex mechanism governing voluntary/involuntary voiding of urinary bladder.

topic: Daily Urea Excretion Quantity & Urine Characteristics
mnemonic: 25 to 30 Grams Urea Daily, pH 6.0 Light Yellow
bullets: Urea Excretion: An adult human excretes on average 25 – 30 grams of urea per day
Physical Properties: Watery fluid, light yellow in color (urochrome), slightly acidic (pH ~6.0)
Clinical Indicators: Glycosuria (Glucose in urine) and Ketonuria (Ketone bodies in urine) indicate Diabetes Mellitus
explanation: Quantitative urinary solute output parameters and key clinical urinalysis diagnostics.

topic: Role of Lungs, Liver, and Skin in Excretion
mnemonic: Lungs CO2, Liver Bile Pigments, Sweat Salt & Urea, Sebaceous Sebum
bullets: Lungs: Remove ~200 mL/minute (18 Litres/day) of CO2 and significant amounts of water
Liver: Secretes bile containing bilirubin, biliverdin, cholesterol, degraded steroid hormones, drugs
Sweat Glands: Excrete NaCl, small amounts of urea, lactic acid
Sebaceous Glands: Eliminate sterols, hydrocarbons, and waxes through sebum
explanation: Accessory excretory organs assisting kidneys in metabolic waste elimination.

mnemonic: Uremia = High Urea Blood, Dialyzing Fluid Lacks Nitrogenous Waste + Heparin
bullets: Uremia: Accumulation of urea in blood due to kidney failure
Hemodialysis: Blood drained from artery mixed with anti-coagulant (Heparin), passed through cellophane tube in dialyzing fluid
Fluid Gradient: Dialyzing fluid has same composition as plasma EXCEPT nitrogenous wastes, allowing waste to diffuse out
Return: Cleared blood pumped back through vein after adding Anti-heparin
explanation: Pathophysiology of renal failure and artificial kidney diffusion mechanism.

bullets: Composition: Stone or insoluble mass of crystallized salts formed within the kidney
Common Molecule: Calcium Oxalate crystals
explanation: Crystalline precipitations forming obstructive mineral deposits in the urinary tract.

bullets: Definition: Inflammatory condition targeting the glomeruli of kidneys
Consequences: Impairs filtration membrane, leading to hematuria (RBCs in urine) and proteinuria
explanation: Immunological or infectious inflammation damaging glomerular capillary filters. Chapter 16: Excretory Products and Their Elimination (30 Mnemonics) 	Page 5

topic: Types of Movement in Human Body Cells
mnemonic: Amoeboid Macrophages, Ciliary Trachea, Muscular Limbs
bullets: Amoeboid: Pseudopodia formed by streaming cytoplasm (e.g., Macrophages and Leucocytes)
Ciliary: Cilia pushing movement in passage (e.g., Trachea clearing dust, Oviducts moving ova)
Muscular: Contraction of muscles for movement (e.g., Limbs, Jaw, Tongue)
explanation: Three principal mechanisms used by human tissues for intracellular and body movements.

topic: Muscle Tissue Proportion in Human Body
mnemonic: 40 to 50 Percent Body Weight is Muscle
bullets: Percentage: 40% – 50% of adult body weight is contributed by muscles
Properties: Excitability, Contractility, Extensibility, and Elasticity
explanation: Total mass contribution and fundamental biological characteristics of muscle tissue.

mnemonic: Skeletal Striated Voluntary, Visceral Smooth Involuntary, Cardiac Branched Striated
bullets: Skeletal: Striated, voluntary, attached to bones, multinucleated (syncytium)
Visceral (Smooth): Non-striated, involuntary, fusiform, uncellular, in visceral organs
Cardiac: Striated, involuntary, branched with intercalated discs in heart wall
explanation: Structural and functional distinction among skeletal, smooth, and cardiac muscular tissues.

mnemonic: Fascia holds Fascicles, Sarcolemma covers Muscle Fibre
bullets: Epimysium / Fascia: Collagenous connective tissue layer holding muscle bundles (fascicles) together
Fascicle: Bundle of muscle fibers (cells) wrapped in perimysium
Sarcolemma: Plasma membrane lining each muscle fiber, enclosing sarcoplasm
explanation: Hierarchical connective tissue layers organizing skeletal muscle bundles into functional units.

topic: Unique Characteristics of Skeletal Muscle Fibre
mnemonic: Syncytium Sarcoplasm, Sarcoplasmic Reticulum Stores Calcium
bullets: Syncytium: Multinucleated state as sarcoplasm contains many nuclei
Sarcoplasmic Reticulum: Specialized endoplasmic reticulum acting as storehouse of Ca2+ ions
Myofibrils: Parallel filaments running lengthwise in sarcoplasm showing alternate dark/light bands
explanation: Cytological specializations essential for calcium handling and longitudinal contraction.

mnemonic: I-band Is Thin Actin (Z-line), A-band Is Thick Myosin (H-zone, M-line)
bullets: I-band (Isotropic): Light band containing Actin (thin filaments), bisected by elastic Z-line
A-band (Anisotropic): Dark band containing Myosin (thick filaments) overlapping actin
H-zone: Central region of A-band NOT overlapped by thin filaments, bisected by thin M-line
explanation: Striation anatomy of sarcomere defining the functional contractile unit between two Z-lines. Chapter 17: Locomotion and Movement (30 Mnemonics) 	Page 1

topic: Structure of Thin Filament (Actin, Tropomyosin, Troponin)
mnemonic: F-Actin Polymer of G-Actin, Tropomyosin Covers Site, Troponin Holds Mask
bullets: F-Actin: Two helically wound filaments composed of monomeric G-actin (Globular actin)
Tropomyosin: Two filaments running close to F-actin along its grooves
Troponin: Complex of 3 subunits distributed at regular intervals; masks myosin-binding sites on actin at rest
explanation: Three-protein molecular architecture regulating actin availability during resting state.

mnemonic: Heavy Meromyosin Head & Arm, Light Meromyosin Tail
bullets: Monomer: Polymerized protein made of Meromyosins
HMM (Heavy Meromyosin): Globular head + short arm; projects outward as cross arm (ATPase + Actin binding site)
LMM (Light Meromyosin): Straight tail portion of meromyosin
explanation: Sub-unit organization of myosin protein establishing motor head and structural tail.

mnemonic: Myosin Head = Active ATPase Enzyme + Actin Binding Site + ATP Site
bullets: ATPase Activity: Head is an active ATPase enzyme that hydrolyzes ATP to ADP + Pi
Binding Sites: Has specific binding site for ATP and binding site for Actin filament
explanation: Functional domains on cross-bridge head driving power strokes during contraction.

mnemonic: Motor Neuron + Muscle Fibre = Motor Unit; Releases Acetylcholine
bullets: Motor Unit: Single motor neuron along with connected muscle fibers
NMJ (Motor End Plate): Junction between motor neuron synaptic knob and sarcolemma of muscle fiber
Neurotransmitter: Release of Acetylcholine generates action potential in sarcolemma
explanation: Synaptic interface converting electrical nerve impulses into muscular activation signals.

topic: Role of Calcium in Muscle Contraction
mnemonic: Action Potential T-Tubule -> Ca2+ Released -> Binds Troponin C -> Unmasks Myosin Site
bullets: Signal: Action potential spreads through sarcolemma and T-tubules into sarcoplasm
Ca2+ Release: SR releases Ca2+ ions into sarcoplasm
Unmasking: Ca2+ binds to Troponin subunit (Troponin C), causing conformational change to unmask binding site on actin
explanation: Excitation-contraction coupling trigger mechanism releasing steric hindrance on actin.

topic: Sliding Filament Theory & Cross Bridge Cycle
mnemonic: Cross Bridge Form -> Power Stroke -> ATP Binds -> Cross Bridge Breaks
bullets: Cross Bridge Formation: Hydrolyzed ATP (ADP+Pi) on myosin head binds unmasked actin
Power Stroke: Myosin pulls actin inwards toward M-line (Z-lines drawn together)
Detachment: New ATP binds myosin head, breaking cross-bridge
explanation: Cyclic molecular steps producing sarcomere shortening without changing filament length. Chapter 17: Locomotion and Movement (30 Mnemonics) 	Page 2

mnemonic: I-band Shortens, H-zone Disappears, A-band Remains Constant
bullets: Reduced / Shortened: I-band reduces in length; H-zone reduces/disappears as actin overlaps
Constant: A-band retains its original length throughout contraction
Distance: Distance between two adjacent Z-lines decreases (Sarcomere shortens)
explanation: Dimensional behavior of sub-sarcomeric bands during filament sliding.

topic: Red Muscle Fibres vs White Muscle Fibres
mnemonic: Red = High Myoglobin, Mitochondria, Slow Fatigue; White = Low Myoglobin, Anaerobic, Fast
bullets: Red Fibres (Aerobic): High myoglobin content, many mitochondria, rich capillaries; slow contraction without fatigue
White Fibres (Anaerobic): Low myoglobin content, few mitochondria, high sarcoplasmic reticulum; fast contraction, fatigues quickly
explanation: Metabolic and contractile dichotomy between slow-twitch aerobic and fast-twitch anaerobic muscle fibers.

topic: Total Number of Bones in Human Skeleton
mnemonic: Axial 80 Bones + Appendicular 126 Bones = 206 Total Bones
bullets: Axial Skeleton: 80 bones distributed along main axis of body
Appendicular Skeleton: 126 bones comprising limbs and supporting girdles
Total: 206 adult bones composed of bone matrix and cartilage
explanation: Divisions and numerical breakdown of the human skeletal system.

mnemonic: Skull 22, Hyoid 1, Ear Ossicles 6, Vertebrae 26, Sternum 1, Ribs 24
bullets: Skull: 22 bones (Cranium 8 + Facial 14)
Hyoid & Ear Ossicles: 1 U-shaped Hyoid + 6 Ear Ossicles (3 in each middle ear)
Vertebral Column: 26 serial units (Adult)
Thoracic Cage: 1 Sternum + 24 Ribs (12 pairs) [Total Axial = 80]
explanation: Comprehensive bone count accounting for all axial components along the body axis.

mnemonic: PEST OF (Parietal, Ethmoid, Sphenoid, Temporal, Occipital, Frontal)
bullets: P: Parietal (2)
E: Ethmoid (1)
S: Sphenoid (1)
T: Temporal (2)
O: Occipital (1) - features 2 occipital condyles (dicondyllic skull)
F: Frontal (1)
explanation: Eight protective bones enclosing the cranial cavity and brain.

mnemonic: Facial 14 Bones + Single U-shaped Hyoid at Base of Buccal Cavity
bullets: Facial Skeleton: 14 bones forming front part of skull (Mandible, Maxillae, Zygomatic, Nasal, Lacrimal, Palatine, Vomer, Inferior Nasal Conchae)
Mandible: Only movable skull bone (except ear ossicles)
Hyoid Bone: Single U-shaped bone located at base of buccal cavity (not articulated with any other bone)
explanation: Anterior skull elements supporting facial structure and tongue attachment. Chapter 17: Locomotion and Movement (30 Mnemonics) 	Page 3

mnemonic: MIS (Malleus, Incus, Stapes) - Hammer, Anvil, Stirrup
bullets: M: Malleus (Hammer-shaped, attached to tympanic membrane)
I: Incus (Anvil-shaped)
S: Stapes (Stirrup-shaped, smallest bone in body, attached to oval window)
explanation: Middle ear ossicular chain amplifying acoustic vibrations toward cochlea.

mnemonic: C7 T12 L5 S(5 fused-1) Co(4 fused-1)
bullets: Cervical (C): 7 (Atlas C1 articulates with occipital condyles; Axis C2)
Thoracic (T): 12
Lumbar (L): 5
Sacral (S): 1 (5 fused in adult)
Coccygeal (Co): 1 (4 fused in adult) [Total adult vertebrae = 26]
explanation: Segmental numerical distribution of vertebral segments protecting spinal cord.

bullets: True Ribs (1–7 pairs): Dorsally attached to thoracic vertebrae, ventrally directly to sternum via hyaline cartilage
False Ribs (8, 9, 10 pairs): Join 7th rib via hyaline cartilage (Vertebrochondral)
Floating Ribs (11, 12 pairs): Ventrally unattached/free
explanation: Classification of 12 pairs of ribs based on ventral attachment to sternum.

topic: Bones of Upper Limb (30 per Limb = 60 Total)
mnemonic: Humerus 1, Radius 1, Ulna 1, Carpals 8, Metacarpals 5, Phalanges 14
bullets: Arm: Humerus (1)
Forearm: Radius (1) + Ulna (1)
Wrist: Carpals (8)
Palm: Metacarpals (5)
Digits: Phalanges (14: formula 2,3,3,3,3) [Total per arm = 30]
explanation: Anatomical order and bone count of forelimb elements from shoulder to fingertips.

topic: Bones of Lower Limb (30 per Limb = 60 Total)
mnemonic: Femur 1, Patella 1, Tibia 1, Fibula 1, Tarsals 7, Metatarsals 5, Phalanges 14
bullets: Thigh: Femur (1, longest & strongest bone)
Knee: Patella (1, sesamoid bone in knee cap)
Shank: Tibia (1) + Fibula (1)
Ankle: Tarsals (7) | Sole: Metatarsals (5) | Toes: Phalanges (14) [Total per leg = 30]
explanation: Anatomical order and bone count of hindlimb elements supporting weight bearing.

mnemonic: Clavicle Collar Bone + Scapula Shoulder Blade (Glenoid Cavity)
bullets: Clavicle (2): Long slender collar bone with 2 curvatures
Scapula (2): Large triangular flat bone on dorsal thorax between 2nd and 7th ribs
Features: Acromion process articulates with clavicle; Glenoid cavity articulates with humerus head
explanation: Pectoral components anchoring upper limbs to axial trunk via mobile articulation. Chapter 17: Locomotion and Movement (30 Mnemonics) 	Page 4

mnemonic: Pelvic Girdle = 2 Coxal Bones (Ilium, Ischium, Pubis) + Acetabulum
bullets: Coxal Bone: Each formed by fusion of 3 bones: Ilium, Ischium, and Pubis
Acetabulum: Deep cavity at fusion point articulating with head of femur
Pubic Symphysis: Joint uniting two halves ventrally containing fibrous cartilage
explanation: Pelvic structure transmitting upper body weight to hindlimbs via stable bony ring.

mnemonic: Fibrous Immovable, Cartilaginous Slightly Movable, Synovial Freely Movable
bullets: Fibrous Joints: No movement (e.g., Sutures between flat skull bones)
Cartilaginous Joints: Limited movement (e.g., Between adjacent vertebrae in spine)
Synovial Joints: Free movement, characterized by fluid-filled synovial cavity
explanation: Structural classification of joints based on tissue medium and degree of mobility.

mnemonic: Ball Shoulder, Hinge Elbow, Pivot Atlas-Axis, Gliding Carpals, Saddle Thumb
bullets: Ball & Socket: Shoulder (Glenoid + Humerus), Hip (Acetabulum + Femur)
Hinge: Elbow joint, Knee joint, Interphalangeal joints
Pivot: Between Atlas (C1) and Axis (C2)
Gliding: Between Carpals in wrist
Saddle: Between Carpal and Metacarpal of Thumb
explanation: Anatomical examples for each major functional subtype of synovial joint.

mnemonic: Myasthenia Autoimmune NMJ Fatigue, Dystrophy Genetic Progressive Degeneration
bullets: Myasthenia Gravis: Autoimmune disorder targeting NMJ receptors; leads to fatigue, weakening, and paralysis of skeletal muscle
Muscular Dystrophy: Progressive degeneration of skeletal muscle, mostly due to genetic mutation (e.g., Duchenne dystrophy)
explanation: Differential clinical etiology between autoimmune neuromuscular failure and hereditary muscle wasting.

mnemonic: Low Ca2+ in Body Fluid Causes Rapid Muscle Spasms (Tetany)
bullets: Definition: Wild, rapid muscle spasms/contractions
Primary Cause: Hypocalcemia (low level of Ca2+ ions in blood/interstitial fluid)
explanation: Electrolyte imbalance causing hyperexcitability of neuromuscular membrane and sustained Spasms.

mnemonic: Arthritis Inflammation, Osteoporosis Low Estrogen Bone Mass, Gout Uric Acid Crystals
bullets: Arthritis: Inflammation of joints
Osteoporosis: Age-related disorder characterized by decreased bone mass, increased fracture risk; common cause is decreased Estrogen level
Gout: Inflammation of joints due to accumulation of Uric Acid crystals
explanation: Key diagnostic pathology distinguishing joint inflammation, bone density loss, and metabolic crystal deposition. Chapter 17: Locomotion and Movement (30 Mnemonics) 	Page 5

mnemonic: Coordination Harmonizes Organs, Neural + Endocrine Control
bullets: Coordination: Process through which two or more organs interact and complement functions of one another
Neural System: Provides point-to-point rapid coordination via nerve impulses
Endocrine System: Provides chemical integration through hormones (slower, long-lasting)
explanation: Fundamental functional contrast between rapid neural signaling and systemic hormonal regulation.

mnemonic: CNS = Brain + Spinal Cord; PNS = Somatic + Autonomic
bullets: Central Nervous System (CNS): Brain and Spinal Cord (site of information processing)
Peripheral Nervous System (PNS): All nerves connecting CNS to body parts
Somatic Nervous System (SNS): Relays impulses from CNS to skeletal muscles (voluntary)
Autonomic Nervous System (ANS): Relays impulses from CNS to involuntary organs & smooth muscles
explanation: Structural and functional hierarchy dividing the central processing unit from peripheral connections.

mnemonic: Sympathetic Fight or Flight, Parasympathetic Rest and Digest
bullets: Sympathetic System: Prepares body for emergency/stress (increases heart rate, dilates pupil)
Parasympathetic System: Promotes vegetative functions (decreases heart rate, stimulates digestion)
explanation: Antagonistic divisions of autonomic neural output maintaining visceral homeostasis.

topic: Types of Nerve Fibres (Afferent vs Efferent)
bullets: Afferent (Sensory) Fibres: Transmit impulses from tissues/organs TO the CNS
Efferent (Motor) Fibres: Transmit regulatory impulses FROM the CNS to effector tissues/organs
explanation: Directional pathways of neural signals relative to the central processing centers.

topic: Structure of Neuron (Cell Body, Dendrites, Axon)
mnemonic: Soma with Nissl Granules, Dendrites Inward, Axon Outward
bullets: Cell Body (Soma): Contains cytoplasm, cell organelles, and Nissl's granules (granular ER + ribosomes)
Dendrites: Short branching fibers containing Nissl's granules; conduct impulses TOWARD cell body
Axon: Long single fiber without Nissl's granules; conducts impulses AWAY from cell body to synapse
explanation: Cytological components and signal directionality across typical multipolar neurons.

mnemonic: Multipolar Cerebral Cortex, Bipolar Retina, Unipolar Embryo
bullets: Multipolar (1 axon + 2/more dendrites): Found in Cerebral Cortex
Bipolar (1 axon + 1 dendrite): Found in Retina of eye and Olfactory epithelium
Unipolar (cell body with 1 axon only): Found usually in Embryonic stage
explanation: Classification based on process count and their characteristic anatomical distribution in the human body. Chapter 18: Neural Control and Coordination (30 Mnemonics) 	Page 1

mnemonic: Schwann Cells Myelin Nodes of Ranvier Cranial Spinal, Unmyelinated Autonomous Somatic
bullets: Myelinated Fibres: Ensheathed with Schwann cells forming myelin sheath; gaps called Nodes of Ranvier (Cranial & Spinal nerves)
Non-Myelinated Fibres: Schwann cell present without myelin sheath formation; lacks Nodes of Ranvier (Autonomous & Somatic neural systems)
explanation: Glial sheath presence and salutatory conduction capacity in different axonal nerve classes.

mnemonic: Resting = High Na+ Outside, High K+ & Negative Proteins Inside (-70 mV)
bullets: Axoplasm: High concentration of K+ and negatively charged proteins, low concentration of Na+
Extracellular Fluid: High concentration of Na+, low concentration of K+
Permeability: Axolemma is more permeable to K+, nearly impermeable to Na+ and negatively charged proteins
Result: Outer surface positive, inner surface negative (Polarised resting potential ~ -70 mV)
explanation: Ionic distribution across resting axonal membrane producing baseline electric polarization.

mnemonic: 3 Na+ Out, 2 K+ In (3 NO 2 KIN)
bullets: Transport: Active transport against concentration gradient requiring ATP
Stoichiometry: Pumps 3 Na+ outwards for every 2 K+ pumped inwards into the cell
Role: Maintains ionic gradients across resting membrane
explanation: Active ion transporter stoichiometry maintaining resting membrane charge inequality.

mnemonic: Stimulus -> Na+ Channels Open -> Rapid Na+ Influx -> Depolarisation (+30 mV)
bullets: Trigger: Threshold stimulus applied at site A makes membrane freely permeable to Na+
Influx: Rapid influx of Na+ causes reversal of polarity (inner surface becomes positive, outer negative)
Action Potential: Electrical potential difference across membrane during depolarisation (~ +30 mV / Nerve Impulse)
explanation: Mechanism of threshold voltage-gated sodium channel activation reversing membrane polarity.

mnemonic: Na+ Channels Close -> K+ Channels Open -> K+ Efflux Restores Resting Potential
bullets: Inactivation: Rise in Na+ permeability is extremely short-lived; Na+ channels close rapidly
Efflux: Voltage-gated K+ channels open, K+ diffuses OUTSIDE axolemma
Result: Restores negative potential inside membrane back to resting state
explanation: Efflux of potassium ions re-establishing resting electronegativity inside the axon.

mnemonic: Current Flows Inside A to B, Outside B to A (Circuit Complete)
bullets: Inner Surface: Current flows from depolarised site A to adjacent site B
Outer Surface: Current flows from site B to site A to complete local circuit
explanation: Local current circuits propelling action potential sequentially along the nerve fiber length. Chapter 18: Neural Control and Coordination (30 Mnemonics) 	Page 2

mnemonic: Electrical Direct Faster Rare, Chemical Gap Synaptic Cleft Slow Common
bullets: Electrical Synapse: Membranes in direct physical contact (gap junctions); impulse flows directly, extremely fast, rare in human body
Chemical Synapse: Separated by fluid-filled Synaptic Cleft; uses neurotransmitters (e.g., Acetylcholine), slower, predominant
explanation: Structural and operational differences between direct electrotonic and transmitter-mediated synaptic transmission.

mnemonic: AP Knob -> Ca2+ Influx -> Vesicle Fusion -> Neurotransmitter Cleft -> Postsynaptic Receptor
bullets: Arrival: Action potential reaches axon terminal / synaptic knob
Calcium: Voltage-gated Ca2+ channels open, Ca2+ influx stimulates synaptic vesicles
Exocytosis: Synaptic vesicles fuse with presynaptic membrane and release neurotransmitter into cleft
Binding: Neurotransmitter binds specific receptors on postsynaptic membrane opening ion channels
explanation: Cascade converting axonal electrical signal into chemical transmitter release across synaptic cleft.

mnemonic: DAP = Dura Mater, Arachnoid, Pia Mater
bullets: D: Dura Mater (Outer, thick, tough fibrous membrane)
A: Arachnoid (Middle, thin web-like layer)
P: Pia Mater (Inner, delicate vascular layer in direct contact with brain tissue)
explanation: Tri-layered protective connective tissue membranes surrounding human brain within cranium.

mnemonic: Forebrain (Cerebrum, Thalamus, Hypo), Midbrain (Corpora), Hindbrain (Pons, Cera, Medulla)
bullets: Forebrain: Cerebrum, Thalamus, and Hypothalamus
Midbrain: Located between Thalamus/Hypothalamus and Pons
Hindbrain: Pons, Cerebellum, and Medulla Oblongata
explanation: Tripartite anatomical division of human brain stem and higher processing centers.

topic: Cerebrum, Corpus Callosum, and Cerebral Cortex
mnemonic: Corpus Callosum Connects Hemispheres, Cortex Grey Outer, Inner White Matter
bullets: Cerebrum: Formed of right & left cerebral hemispheres connected by nerve tract bundle called Corpus Callosum
Cerebral Cortex: Outer neuron cell body layer (Grey matter due to greyish appearance)
Inner Medulla: Myelinated axon tracts giving white opaque appearance (White matter)
explanation: Gross structure of cerebrum, interhemispheric commissure, and cellular distribution in cortex.

mnemonic: Motor Area, Sensory Area, Association Area (Memory & Communication)
bullets: Motor Area: Controls voluntary motor movements
Sensory Area: Receives sensory inputs
Association Area: Neither clearly sensory nor motor; responsible for complex functions like intersensory associations, memory, and communication
explanation: Functional zoning of cerebral cortex into dedicated input, output, and integrative processing fields. Chapter 18: Neural Control and Coordination (30 Mnemonics) 	Page 3

mnemonic: Hypothalamus = Thermoregulation, Hunger, Thirst, Pituitary Hormones
bullets: Center: Controls body temperature, urge for eating (hunger) and drinking (thirst)
Neurosecretory Cells: Contains groups of neurosecretory cells secreting hypothalamic hormones controlling pituitary gland
explanation: Diencephalic center regulating vital vegetative drives, body temperature, and endocrine master control.

mnemonic: Amygdala + Hippocampus = Limbic System (Emotion, Rage, Motivation, Sexual Behaviour)
bullets: Structures: Inner parts of cerebral hemispheres + group of deep structures like Amygdala and Hippocampus
Functions: Regulation of sexual behavior, expression of emotional reactions (excitement, pleasure, rage, fear), and motivation
explanation: Subcortical neural network driving emotional states, memory consolidation, and instinctive behaviors.

mnemonic: Cerebral Aqueduct Passes Midbrain, Corpora Quadrigemina 4 Dorsal Lobes
bullets: Canal: Cerebral Aqueduct passes through the midbrain
Tectum: Dorsal portion consists of 4 round swellings (lobes) called Corpora Quadrigemina (visual and auditory reflex centers)
explanation: Midbrain anatomical landmarks regulating visual tracking and acoustic startle reflexes.

mnemonic: Pons Fibres, Cerebellum Balance, Medulla Vital Controls; Brainstem = Midbrain + Pons + Medulla
bullets: Pons: Consists of fiber tracts interconnecting different regions of brain
Cerebellum: Highly convoluted surface providing extra space for many more neurons (controls balance and coordination)
Medulla: Controls respiration, cardiovascular reflexes, and gastric secretions
Brain Stem: Midbrain + Pons + Medulla Oblongata (connects brain to spinal cord)
explanation: Hindbrain subdivisions and vital brainstem axis maintaining involuntary survival functions.

mnemonic: Receptor -> Afferent Neuron -> Interneuron/CNS -> Efferent Neuron -> Effector Organ
bullets: Receptor: Detects stimulus
Afferent Neuron: Transmits signal via dorsal nerve root into CNS
Interneuron/CNS: Processes impulse in spinal cord gray matter
Efferent Neuron: Carries motor signal via ventral root to effector organ (muscle/gland)
explanation: Five-element neuronal pathway executing rapid involuntary protective responses.

mnemonic: Patellar Tendon Stretch -> Monosynaptic Pathway -> Extensor Muscles Contract
bullets: Stimulus: Tapping patellar tendon stretches muscle spindle
Pathway: Afferent neuron synapses directly with motor neuron in spinal cord (monosynaptic pathway)
Response: Motor signal causes contraction of quadriceps, causing leg extension
explanation: Classic clinical stretch reflex illustrating simple monosynaptic spinal circuit execution. Chapter 18: Neural Control and Coordination (30 Mnemonics) 	Page 4

topic: Structure of Eye Wall (3 Layers Outer to Inner)
mnemonic: Sclera Fibrous, Choroid Vascular, Retina Neural
bullets: Outer Layer: Sclera (dense connective tissue); anterior transparent portion is Cornea
Middle Layer: Choroid (vascular, bluish color); forms Ciliary Body and Iris anteriorly
Inner Layer: Retina (contains photoreceptor cells, bipolar cells, ganglion cells)
explanation: Concentric structural coats of the eyeball enclosing ocular fluids and lens assembly.

mnemonic: Rods Twilight Rhodopsin Vitamin A, Cones Daylight Red Green Blue Color
bullets: Rods: Twilight (scotopic) vision; contain purplish-red protein Rhodopsin (visual purple, derivative of Vitamin A)
Cones: Daylight (photopic) vision & color vision; three types sensitive to Red, Green, and Blue light
explanation: Photoreceptor cell dichotomy governing low-light monochrome vs bright-light color perception.

mnemonic: Blind Spot No Photoreceptors Optic Nerve Exits, Fovea Only Cones Max Acuity
bullets: Blind Spot: Point where optic nerve leaves eyeball and retinal blood vessels enter; lacks photoreceptors
Macula Lutea & Fovea: Yellowish spot with central thinned-out pit (Fovea); contains densely packed CONES only, area of highest visual acuity
explanation: Retinal topographic specializations marking optic nerve exit vs maximum resolution center.

mnemonic: Light -> Retinal Dissociates from Opsin -> Structural Change -> Bipolar -> Ganglion -> Optic Nerve
bullets: Photopigment: Rhodopsin consists of Opsin (protein) + Retinal (aldehyde of Vitamin A)
Dissociation: Light induces dissociation of Retinal from Opsin, changing Opsin structure
Signal: Membrane permeability changes generate potential difference across bipolar and ganglion cells
explanation: Photochemical cascade converting light photon absorption into action potential train along optic nerve.

topic: Anatomical Structure of Ear (External, Middle, Inner)
mnemonic: External Pinna Meatus, Middle Ossicles Eustachian, Inner Cochlea Organ of Corti
bullets: External Ear: Pinna + External Auditory Meatus (tympanic membrane/eardrum)
Middle Ear: Malleus, Incus, Stapes + Eustachian tube (connects middle ear cavity to pharynx to equalize pressure)
Inner Ear (Labyrinth): Fluid-filled membranous labyrinth inside bony labyrinth
explanation: Tripartite auditory architecture transferring acoustic pressure waves into fluid vibration.

mnemonic: Cochlea Hearing Organ of Corti, Vestibular Crista & Macula Balance
bullets: Cochlea: Coiled auditory organ; Organ of Corti located on basilar membrane contains hair cells acting as auditory receptors
Vestibular Apparatus: Composed of 3 Semicircular Canals + Otolith Organ (Saccule and Utricle)
Receptors for Balance: Crista ampullaris (in semicircular canals for dynamic balance) + Macula (in otoliths for static balance)
explanation: Dual inner ear specializations for sound transduction and vestibular equilibrium maintenance. Chapter 18: Neural Control and Coordination (30 Mnemonics) 	Page 5

topic: Definition and Modern Concept of Hormones
mnemonic: Hormones = Non-Nutrient Intercellular Messengers Produced in Trace Amounts
bullets: Traditional definition: Chemicals produced by endocrine glands poured directly into blood
Modern definition: Non-nutrient chemicals acting as intercellular messengers produced in trace amounts
Scope: Includes hormones secreted by organized endocrine glands as well as non-endocrine tissues (heart, kidney, GI tract)
explanation: Evolution of hormone definition incorporating local and systemic non-endocrine signaling molecules.

topic: Major Endocrine Glands in Human Body
mnemonic: HPTP TAG O P Adrenal - Hypothalamus, Pituitary, Pineal, Thyroid, Thymus, Adrenal, Gonads, Pancreas
bullets: Hypothalamus, Pituitary, Pineal, Thyroid, Parathyroid, Thymus, Adrenal gland
Pancreas (Islets of Langerhans) and Gonads (Testis in males, Ovary in females)
Scattered endocrine cells also present in gastric, duodenal, renal, and cardiac tissues
explanation: Comprehensive anatomical checklist of primary ductless endocrine glands in humans.

mnemonic: Releasing Hormones Stimulate, Inhibiting Hormones Stop (e.g., Somatostatin)
bullets: Releasing Hormones (RH): Stimulate secretion of pituitary hormones (e.g., GnRH stimulates gonadotrophins)
Inhibiting Hormones (IH): Inhibit secretion of pituitary hormones (e.g., Somatostatin inhibits growth hormone)
Portal System: Hypothalamic hormones reach anterior pituitary via hypophyseal portal system
explanation: Dual control mechanism exercised by hypothalamic neurosecretory nuclei over anterior pituitary.

mnemonic: Adenohypophysis = Pars Distalis + Pars Intermedia; Neurohypophysis = Pars Nervosa
bullets: Adenohypophysis (Anterior Pituitary): Divided into pars distalis and pars intermedia
Neurohypophysis (Posterior Pituitary): Known as pars nervosa; stores and releases oxytocin and vasopressin
explanation: Embryological and structural division of the pituitary gland into anterior and posterior lobes.

mnemonic: FLAT PEG - FSH, LH, ACTH, TSH, Prolactin, Endorphins/MSH, GH
bullets: TSH (Thyroid Stimulating Hormone), ACTH (Adrenocorticotropic Hormone)
LH (Luteinizing Hormone), FSH (Follicle Stimulating Hormone)
Prolactin (PRL) and Growth Hormone (GH)
Pars Intermedia secretes Melanocyte Stimulating Hormone (MSH) in humans (merged with pars distalis)
explanation: Classic mnemonic for memorizing all six major anterior pituitary trophic hormones.

mnemonic: Dwarfism = Low GH Children, Gigantism = High GH Children, Acromegaly = High GH Adults
bullets: Dwarfism: Stunted growth due to hyposecretion of GH during childhood
Gigantism: Abnormal overgrowth due to hypersecretion of GH during childhood
Acromegaly: Disproportionate facial/limb enlargement due to GH hypersecretion in adults
explanation: Pathological consequences of growth hormone imbalance across different age stages. Chapter 19: Chemical Coordination and Integration (30 Mnemonics) 	Page 1

mnemonic: Prolactin = Milk Production, TSH = Thyroid Stimulator, ACTH = Adrenal Cortex Stimulator
bullets: Prolactin: Regulates growth of mammary glands and formation of milk in females
TSH: Stimulates synthesis and secretion of thyroid hormones from thyroid gland
ACTH: Stimulates synthesis and secretion of glucocorticoid hormones from adrenal cortex
explanation: Primary trophic functions of prolactin, thyrotrophin, and adrenocorticotrophin.

bullets: Luteinizing Hormone (LH): Stimulates ovulation in females and synthesis/secretion of androgens (testosterone) in males
Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH): Stimulates growth of ovarian follicles in females and spermatogenesis in males
explanation: Gonadotrophic regulation of gametogenesis and sex steroid synthesis in testes and ovaries.

mnemonic: Oxytocin = Childbirth/Milk Ejection, ADH = Water Reabsorption in Kidney
bullets: Oxytocin: Contracts smooth muscles; stimulates uterine contraction during child birth and milk ejection from mammary glands
Vasopressin (ADH): Acts mainly at renal tubules stimulating resorption of water and electrolytes, reducing water loss (diuresis)
explanation: Neurohypophyseal hormones synthesized by hypothalamus and released into posterior pituitary.

mnemonic: DI = Low ADH -> Excessive Dilute Urine + Intense Thirst (Polyuria + Polydipsia)
bullets: Cause: Deficiency of Vasopressin / Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH)
Symptoms: Inability of kidneys to conserve water leading to water loss, frequent urination (polyuria), and severe thirst
explanation: Endocrine disorder resulting from impaired water reabsorption in renal distal nephrons.

mnemonic: Pineal = Melatonin, Circadian Rhythm, Sleep-Wake Cycle, Pigmentation
bullets: Location: Dorsal side of forebrain
Hormone: Melatonin (plays vital role in regulating 24-hour circadian rhythm of body)
Functions: Maintains sleep-wake cycle, body temperature, metabolism, pigmentation, and defense capability
explanation: Epiphysis cerebri hormone dictating biological rhythms and photoperiodic responses.

mnemonic: Thyroid = Isthmus Connects Lobes, Follicles Filled with Thyroglobulin + T3/T4
bullets: Structure: Two lobes on either side of trachea connected by non-secretory tissue called isthmus
Histology: Composed of follicles and stromal tissues; thyroid follicles filled with colloid (T3 and T4)
explanation: Gross and microscopic structure of the butterfly-shaped endocrine gland in the neck. Chapter 19: Chemical Coordination and Integration (30 Mnemonics) 	Page 2

topic: Thyroid Hormones (T3, T4) and Iodine Requirement
mnemonic: Thyroxine Requires Iodine; Regulates Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR), RBC Formation
bullets: Requirement: Iodine is essential for normal rate of hormone synthesis in thyroid
Functions: Regulates BMR, supports RBC formation, controls carbohydrate, protein, and fat metabolism
Thyrocalcitonin (TCT): Protein hormone secreted by thyroid reducing blood calcium levels (hypocalcemic)
explanation: Metabolic control and iodine dependence of thyroid follicular hormone synthesis.

mnemonic: Hypothyroidism = Goitre (Low Iodine), Cretinism (Stunted Child), Myxedema (Adult)
bullets: Simple Goitre: Enlargement of thyroid gland due to dietary iodine deficiency
Cretinism: Hypothyroidism during pregnancy causing stunted growth, mental retardation, abnormal skin
Myxedema: Hypothyroidism in adult women causing low BMR and weight gain
explanation: Clinical syndromes resulting from inadequate thyroid hormone production.

mnemonic: Graves = Bulging Eyes (Exophthalmos) + High BMR + Weight Loss
bullets: Cause: Hypersecretion of thyroid hormones due to thyroid cancer or nodules
Symptoms: Enlarged thyroid, high BMR, increased heart rate, nervousness, weight loss, protruding eyeballs
explanation: Autoimmune hyperthyroid condition characterized by accelerated metabolism and exophthalmos.

mnemonic: PTH = Increases Blood Ca2+ (Hypercalcemic), Stimulates Bone Resorption
bullets: Location: 4 small glands stuck on back side of thyroid lobes
Parathyroid Hormone (PTH): Peptide hormone increasing blood calcium levels (hypercalcemic factor)
Action: Stimulates bone resorption (demineralization), promotes Ca2+ reabsorption by renal tubules and absorption from digested food
explanation: Calcium homeostasis regulator acting antagonistically to thyrocalcitonin.

mnemonic: Thymus = Behind Sternum, Thymosins Mediate Cell-Mediated Immunity (T-Lymphocytes)
bullets: Location: Lobular structure located between lungs behind sternum on aorta
Hormone: Thymosins (peptide hormones playing major role in cell-mediated immunity)
Differentiation: Promotes differentiation of T-lymphocytes for cell-mediated immunity and antibodies for humoral immunity
explanation: Immuno-endocrine gland promoting T-cell maturation that degenerates with age.

mnemonic: Adrenal on Kidneys: Outer Cortex (3 zones), Inner Medulla (Adrenaline)
bullets: Structure: Situated on anterior top of each kidney; composed of outer cortex and inner medulla
Cortex Zones (Outer to Inner): Zona glomerulosa (mineralocorticoids), Zona fasciculata (glucocorticoids), Zona reticularis (sex corticoids)
explanation: Zonal organization and dual embryological origin of adrenal glands. Chapter 19: Chemical Coordination and Integration (30 Mnemonics) 	Page 3

mnemonic: Cortisol = Gluconeogenesis, Aldosterone = Na+ Retention & Water Balance
bullets: Glucocorticoids (Cortisol): Involved in carbohydrate metabolism, stimulates gluconeogenesis, lipolysis, proteolysis, anti-inflammatory
Mineralocorticoids (Aldosterone): Regulates water and electrolyte balance; acts at renal tubules to reabsorb Na+ and water, excrete K+/PO43-
Androgenic Corticoids: Secreted in small amounts, stimulate axial/pubic hair growth during puberty
explanation: Primary steroid hormones secreted by adrenal cortex regulating metabolism and electrolytes.

mnemonic: Addison = Hypo-cortisol (Low BP, Pigmentation), Cushing = Hyper-cortisol (Moon face, High BP)
bullets: Addison's Disease: Underproduction of hormones by adrenal cortex causing hypoglycemia, weakness, skin pigmentation
Cushing's Syndrome: Overproduction of cortisol causing obesity, moon face, high blood pressure, hyperglycemia
