explanation: Clinical contrasting disorders of adrenal cortical insufficiency versus excess.

mnemonic: Adrenaline + Noradrenaline = Fight or Flight Hormones (Emergency Response)
bullets: Hormones: Adrenaline (Epinephrine) and Noradrenaline (Norepinephrine) collectively called catecholamines
Trigger: Secreted in response to stress, emergency, fear, or danger (Fight or Flight)
Effects: Increases heart rate, heart contraction strength, respiration rate, pupil dilation, and breakdown of glycogen
explanation: Sympathomimetic hormones preparing the body for rapid physical emergency action.

topic: Pancreas as Composite Gland (Islets of Langerhans)
bullets: Composite Gland: Acts as both exocrine (digestive enzymes) and endocrine (Islets of Langerhans, 1-2% of tissue)
Alpha Cells: Secrete Glucagon (increases blood glucose by glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis)
Beta Cells: Secrete Insulin (decreases blood glucose by cellular uptake and glycogenesis)
explanation: Endocrine pancreas cell types maintaining strict blood glucose homeostasis.

mnemonic: DM = Low Insulin Resistance -> High Blood Glucose (Hyperglycemia) + Glycosuria
bullets: Cause: Prolonged hyperglycemia due to insulin deficiency or receptor resistance
Symptoms: Loss of glucose in urine (glycosuria) and formation of ketone bodies
Treatment: Insulin therapy and dietary management
explanation: Metabolic disorder characterized by impaired carbohydrate utilization and chronic hyperglycemia.

mnemonic: Testis Leydig Cells Produce Testosterone; Regulates Spermatogenesis & Secondary Sex Characters
bullets: Location: Leydig (interstitial) cells present in intertubular spaces of testis
Hormone: Androgens (primarily testosterone)
Functions: Regulates maturation of male accessory sex organs, spermatogenesis, libido, and secondary sexual characters
explanation: Male gonadal steroidogenesis driving primary and secondary sexual maturation. Chapter 19: Chemical Coordination and Integration (30 Mnemonics) 	Page 4

mnemonic: Ovary = Graafian Follicle makes Estrogen, Corpus Luteum makes Progesterone
bullets: Estrogen: Synthesized by growing ovarian follicles; stimulates growth of female secondary sex organs and uterine changes
Progesterone: Secreted by corpus luteum; supports pregnancy, maintains endometrium, and stimulates mammary gland milk secretion
explanation: Female sex steroid hormones orchestrating menstrual cycle, pregnancy, and secondary characters.

topic: Hormones of Heart, Kidney, and GI Tract
mnemonic: Heart ANF (Lowers BP), Kidney EPO (RBC), GI Tract Gastrin/Secretin (Digestion)
bullets: Atrial Wall: Secretes Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF) which decreases blood pressure by vasodilation
Juxtaglomerular Cells of Kidney: Produce Erythropoietin (EPO) which stimulates erythropoiesis (RBC formation)
Gastrointestinal Tract: Secretes peptide hormones Gastrin, Secretin, CCK, and GIP regulating digestive secretions
explanation: Non-endocrine organ endocrine secretions coordinating systemic circulation and digestion.

mnemonic: Peptide Hormones = Membrane Receptors (Second Messengers); Steroid Hormones = Intracellular Receptors (Gene Expression)
bullets: Membrane-bound Receptors: For water-soluble hormones (peptide, protein, amines); generate second messengers (cAMP, IP3, Ca2+)
Intracellular Receptors: For lipid-soluble hormones (steroids, iodothyronines); directly interact with DNA to regulate gene expression
explanation: Biochemical classification of hormone receptor localization and signal transduction pathways.

mnemonic: Hormone (1st Messenger) -> Receptor -> cAMP (2nd Messenger) -> Biochemical Response
bullets: First Messenger: Hormone binding to membrane receptor outside cell
Second Messenger: Generated inside cell (e.g., cAMP, Ca2+, IP3) to regulate cellular metabolism
Amplification: Cascade of enzyme reactions producing rapid physiological response
explanation: Signal amplification cascade utilized by hydrophilic protein and peptide hormones.

mnemonic: Steroid Crosses Membrane -> Binds Nuclear Receptor -> Hormone-Receptor Complex -> Genome Interaction -> Protein Synthesis
bullets: Transport: Lipid-soluble steroid hormones easily cross cell membrane
Nuclear Binding: Bind intracellular receptors inside nucleus
Response: Hormone-receptor complex interacts with genome to control gene expression and protein synthesis (slower, long-lasting)
explanation: Direct genomic mechanism of action characteristic of steroid and thyroid hormones.

mnemonic: Negative Feedback Inhibits, Positive Feedback Amplifies Hormone Output
bullets: Negative Feedback: High level of target hormone inhibits pituitary/hypothalamic release (most common homeostatic loop)
Positive Feedback: Hormone release stimulates further production (e.g., oxytocin surge during childbirth)
explanation: Homeostatic regulatory loops maintaining precise hormonal balance in human body. Chapter 19: Chemical Coordination and Integration (30 Mnemonics) 	Page 5
